newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH CEMENT MAKERS FIGHT FOR CONCRETE MOTORWAYS.
newsitem.headline: POLISH CEMENT MAKERS FIGHT FOR CONCRETE MOTORWAYS.

text.p: Poland's cement lobby urged the government on Wednesday to declare that a planned 2,500 km of new motorways should be build of concrete and not asphalt.
"Concrete motorways last longer and are less trouble to use," Andrzej Tekiel, deputy chairman of the Association of Cement and Lime Producers, grouping cement plant managers, told a news conference.
"By not taking such measures the state treasury... deprives itself of control over technical conditions in which the motorways will be built," he added.
The cement sector hopes to benefit from the scheme to build some 2,500 km of toll motorways within the next 15 years.
The programme in its current shape allows international consortia that win tenders to build more than a dozen motorway sections to choose between concrete and asphalt.
